content: Firestore transactions use optimistic concurrency on web/mobile SDKs: the transaction tracks every document read and only commits if none changed, otherwise it retries a finite number of times (firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/manage-data/transactions and cloud.google.com transaction-data-contention). A check-then-write outside a transaction is not atomic: two clients performing a non-transactional get() then set() will both see 'empty' and one will overwrite the other (varstatt.com Firestore transactions practice writeup). firebase-js-sdk issue #6659 documents an 'Document already exists' failure without retry fixed in v9.14.0. Security rules can enforce singleton invariants with request.resource plus getAfter().
